name: DecryptedText-TS-TW
title: Decrypted Text
description: A line of text flickers through random letters and punctuation before resolving character by character into the real sentence. It can start on hover, when scrolled into view, or on a click.
use: A tech or sci-fi page wants a heading to feel encoded and then resolve, without a full typewriter.
avoid: Constant glyph swapping hurts readability and is motion-heavy; poor for long body copy or calm pages.
a11y: The real sentence is exposed to screen readers through sr-only text, but the pointer triggers are not focusable. (keyboard: no, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Three lines of bold text stack down a black stage: a large green heading, a medium blue monospaced line and a smaller purple line. Every character keeps its slot, so during the run each word shows some settled letters and some random glyphs.
behaves: Hovering the first line makes it scrambles then resolve; the second decrypts once as it scrolls into view; the third toggles between plain text and a scramble on each click. While running, a timer swaps unrevealed characters for random glyphs until the true text is restored.
customise: Set text, speed and maxIterations, choose hover, view, in-view-hover or click, pick a start, end or centre reveal, and supply a character pool or reuse only the original letters.
weight: moderate: One interval re-renders a span per character about every 50ms while running.
